rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, so headings should default to claims. Three of four do: 'Durable state keeps the place', 'Feedback keeps the direction', and 'A boundary decides whether to continue' are each a declarative answer to their own implicit question. The fourth, l.29 'What stops a long run before done-done', is phrased as a question rather than an answer -- the closest line in this file to tripping the rule, since it breaks the other three headers' own pattern. It stays inside because the maintainer block names and defends exactly this inversion as deliberate: l.47 'The fourth slide (2026-08-14, Antti-directed) inverts the lecture's own frame, and its roster is a maintainer call. Three slides answer what keeps a run going; this one asks what ends it ahead of done-done, which is the question a student can act on...'. That is a documented accept-note on this exact header's grammar, and the interrogative form also mirrors the file's own H1 ('What keeps a long-running session going?'), so it does not read as an exercise-style imperative or phase label -- the harm the rule guards against (mood confusion between instruction and stated law) is not present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 14 bullets plus the blockquote and the closing kicker against the three classes. Closest candidate, still inside: l.26 'The question is not how many checks the repo has. It is what notices first when this particular session goes wrong.' reads aphoristic but adds a genuinely new analytical move (a triage question) beyond l.25's enumeration, not a doctrine restatement of the header. l.11 'Durable state needs a home and an owner...' likewise adds a new actionable criterion (home + owner) rather than re-announcing 'durable state keeps the place'. The l.37 kicker ('When your agent stops for missing information, check whether there was a way for it to uncover that. Usually there was.') is not a (c)-class aphorism-kicker restating the header or a `**The point:**` line -- it gives a new, specific checking behaviour tied to one bullet, and the maintainer block (l.47) defends it in exactly those terms ('turns the whole slide from a taxonomy into something the student does on return'). No (b)-class self-referential design commentary found -- l.11's 'not memory the system can trust' is a claim about the student's own repo hygiene, not commentary about this curriculum's pedagogy.
